extracted.intended_audience: piano teachers, advanced piano students, and professional pianists interested in pedagogy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for piano teaching, technical development, practice, and musical interpretation aimed at producing competent, expressive pianists. Covers foundational exercises, technique, practice habits, interpretive principles, and pedagogical method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of technical work from study of music
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate the technical training at the outset from the study of music itself to secure the most perfect foundation and later the best results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach mechanics and relaxation first (hand, wrist, arm, thumb control) before extensive musical study; use monthly classes and supervised group/pupil classes to monitor technical work and ensure consistent progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performing from memory in class
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything is played from memory in class; no printed notes are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Playing from memory is difficult at first (concentration issues) but becomes easier with practice; use class recitals and peer performance to strengthen memorization and focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand and arm posture (arched hands, curved fingers, loose wrists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hands should be well arched at the knuckles, fingers curved with adequate action at the knuckle joint; wrists in normal position and extremely loose; the whole arm should swing from the shoulder and be poised over the keys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This posture enables proper weight distribution for every note, fuller singing tone, and is exemplified even in young pupils; avoid stiff wrists and cramped hand positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of arm weight and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Every note should have its amount of hand or arm weight; place released arm weight where appropriate and eliminate where not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish the principle of 'weight' early; after relaxation is achieved, learn to deploy arm weight for tone, power, and variety of effects rather than relying on finger force alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundational 'table work' exercises and sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with table work: about ten exercises embodying principles of piano playing, progressing from large arm motions to small finger actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence: form arched hand and thumb control → combined arm and wrist rotary movements → hand staccato from wrist → finger action exercises (one to five fingers in combinations) → trills, scales, arpeggios, chords, octaves, double notes. Emphasize relaxation first, then strengthening, then finger action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotary movement and thumb/finger control
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach each finger with rotary movement of arm and wrist; thumb must be taught to move properly for control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold each finger firmly in curved position and develop rotary motions before isolated finger technique; this builds independence and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staccato mechanism (hand staccato via wrist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand staccato is produced by hand action at the wrist and includes an element of percussion for directness and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop staccato via wrist motion rather than finger-only percussion to achieve directness without loss of musicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression from general to particular in technical training
rubrics_metrics.description: Work from larger free-arm movements to smaller finger movements (from 'general to the particular'), not the reverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish global relaxation and large motions first so smaller, precise finger mechanisms can be built on a relaxed foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of studies/etudes for technical development
rubrics_metrics.description: Use studies frequently (from various composers/opuses) above early grades; studies treat definite technical principles in many ways and are often more valuable than pieces for technical development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select studies appropriate to grade (Duvernoy, Berens, Czerny Op.740, Heller, Foote, MacDowell, Harberbrier, Kessler, Moszkowski, Henselt, Rubinstein, Chopin, Liszt). Studies need not be memorized but must be played with the finish of a piece to derive maximum benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended pedagogical reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain books aid the teacher's understanding of education and psychology and are helpful to pedagogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested works include Dr. Herman H. Home's The Philosophy of Education and The Psychology of Education, and William James' Talks to Teachers on Psychology; teachers should study educational and psychological principles to inform instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic awakening of thought (head, hand, heart)
rubrics_metrics.description: Piano study must awaken thought and give a wider outlook; the trinity of factors in playing are head, hand, and heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stimulate pupils' interests beyond mechanics—expose them to art, literature, science, and spiritual ideas so playing is expressive and intellectual, not merely mechanical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation teaching: avoid pedantry; illustrate conceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid pedantry; present your own conception as 'I see or feel it in this way' and give underlying reasons; illustrate nuances rather than merely tell them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teacher should be a pianist capable of demonstrating; explain reasons behind interpretive choices, show subtle color, phrasing, and bravura effects by playing, and guide pupils towards understanding the composer's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of personality in performance
rubrics_metrics.description: A player's personality should enter performance only insofar as the performance remains true to the composer's intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personality that illuminates and adds charm is good; personality that obstructs the composer's meaning or calls attention to itself is vanity and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced technic: weight and finger action
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach both high finger action and pressure touch once arm-weight principles are established; use high finger action only to develop independence and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for freedom of body, arm and wrist, a firm arched hand, and set fingers that allow control for power, velocity, or delicacy as needed—'virtue is the happy mean between two vices.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice amount and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Four hours of concentrated work daily is generally sufficient; quality of practice matters more than quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize thinking and listening rather than mindless repetition; take pauses to reflect on meaning; stop after several repetitions to think and refresh ears and hands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand position debate: fingers close to keys versus high lifting
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping fingers close to the keyboard and pressing gives a warmer, more elastic tone; high lifting can produce harsh tone and interfere with smoothness and velocity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate a loose wrist and natural curved fingertip position rather than forced straight-line fingertip placement at the key edge; avoid forced or unnatural hand positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginner prerequisites and early curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning pupils should learn note values, rhythm, time, ear-training and understand the piano mechanism before attempting to play much.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain clearly what to do to make a musical tone; stress ‘never touch the piano without trying to make music’; teach form and shape as movement toward cadences and climaxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key mechanism and touch principles (Matthay's rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for touch: (a) make the hammer-end of key move to make sound; (b) swifter movement → louder sound; (c) gradual swiftness → more beautiful tone; (d) for brilliant tone hit the string via the key, not the key itself; (e) 'aim' the key to the beginning of each sound; (f) never squeeze the key beds; (g) feel the giving-way point of the key.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always feel key resistance and listen for the precise moment the sound begins so effort is directed to sound production rather than mechanical key depression; avoid hitting or squeezing keys which impedes tone and agility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnosis and correction of faults
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching must not only point out faults but make clear the cause of each fault and the way to correct it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete corrective steps and exercises rather than vague criticism; analyze underlying muscular or conceptual errors that produce the fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubato: bending not breaking time
rubrics_metrics.description: True rubato is the bending of the time but not breaking it; extra time given to certain notes must be compensated by taking time from others to even things up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate rubato with musical examples; avoid treating rubato as arbitrary tempo breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedaling: judicious use of damper pedal
rubrics_metrics.description: Misuse of the damper pedal can ruin phrasing and tonal effects crafted by the fingers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach pedaling with numerous illustrations and by close attention to the actual sounds produced; pedal only with an ear to clarity and phrasing, not to mask poor finger technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forearm rotation and muscular coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct forearm rotary exertion is necessary for many effects and should be understood; there are two opposite forms of technic implied by 'flat' and 'bent' finger actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain where rotary action applies and how it contributes to tone, agility, and prevention of incorrect muscular habits; include exercises to develop correct forearm rotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive teacher's method: accretion and individualization
rubrics_metrics.description: The progressive teacher's method must be one of accretion: gain ideas from many methods, assimilate and make them practical, originate and adapt for individual pupils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pupils with personalized blank books of adapted exercises; draw selectively from Leschetizky, Virgil, Mason, Matthay, and others, modifying principles to suit each pupil's requirements.
